title: The Zelevinsky involution, co-standard modules for quantum affine algebras and interval symmetric functions
summary:
Let $\mathscr{F}_n$ be the subcategory of finite-dimensional representations of the quantum loop algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$ whose simple modules are indexed by multisegments consisting of intervals $[a,b]$, where $a,b$ are integers and $0<b-a\le n$. We define the co-standard module associated to a multisegment $\mathbf{s}$ to be the tensor product of the Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules, associated to the first node of the Dynkin diagram of $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$, given by the segments of $\mathbf{s}$. Under a suitable (and necessary) restriction on $n$, we show that its socle is isomorphic to the simple module given by the Zelevinsky dual $\mathbf{s}^\dagger$ of $\mathbf{s}$. We then define an involution $Φ$ of the Grothendieck ring $\mathcal{K}(\mathscr {F}_n)$ and prove that it maps the class of a simple module to the class of the simple module given by its Zelevinsky dual. We also show that on suitable subcategories $Φ$ is induced by an exact autoequivalence reversing tensor products, and we give a $t$-analogue of the multiplicity identity in the quantum Grothendieck ring.
  Motivated by the determinantal formula for alternating snake modules, we realize $\mathcal{K}(\mathscr {F}_n)$ explicitly inside a polynomial ring in variables indexed by intervals, and, in the spirit of Macdonald's ninth variation of Schur functions, we show that the fundamental modules correspond to analogues of the elementary symmetric functions and the Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules to analogues of the complete homogeneous symmetric functions. This is compatible with $Φ$ and the classical involution $ω$, and we prove that alternating snake modules give a family of Schur positive symmetric functions extending the skew Schur functions.

title: Root vector localization and minimal nilpotent finite $W$-algebras
summary:
Let \(\mathfrak{g}\) be any finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra, let $h^\vee$ be its dual Coxeter number, and let \(e\) be its highest-root vector which is a minimal nilpotent element. In this paper, using a result of Bavula on invariants of commuting locally nilpotent derivations, we show that \[
  U(\mathfrak{g})_f
  \cong \mathcal{D}^+_{h^\vee-2}\otimes \mathcal{D}_1\otimes U(\mathfrak{g},e), \]
  where the first factor is a polynomial Weyl algebra of rank $h^\vee-2$, the second factor is a Laurent Weyl algebra of rank one, and $U(\mathfrak{g},e)$ is the finite $W$-algebra associated with $\mathfrak{g}$ and $e$. As an application, we prove that if $M$ is a simple infinite-dimensional $\mathfrak{g}$-module with the minimal GK dimension on which $f-1$ acts locally nilpotently, then $M\cong P\otimes V$ for some simple $\mathcal{D}^+_{h^\vee-2}\otimes \mathcal{D}_1$-module $P$ and some finite-dimensional simple $U(\mathfrak{g},e)$-module $V$. We also give a new proof of the Skryabine quivalence and Petukhov's birational decomposition of the quotient division ring of $U(\mathfrak{g})$.

title: Stable equivalence of quadratic monomial algebras
summary: It is well known that gentle algebras are closed under derived equivalence. However, it is easy to verify that they are not closed under stable equivalence. We prove that the classes of quadratic monomial, almost gentle and string almost gentle algebras are closed under stable equivalence. In fact, in each of these cases, stable equivalence is characterized by isomorphism after deleting all nodes and removing semisimple direct summands. The underlying isomorphism theorem gives a positive answer to Martínez-Villa's question on selfinjective-free algebras for these classes. We also prove that the nonprojective simple modules form the unique weakly simple-minded system of a quadratic monomial algebra. Consequently, every stable equivalence of Morita type involving such an algebra lifts to a Morita equivalence when neither algebra has semisimple direct summands. Finally, we describe the effect of node deletion on stable categories of Gorenstein-projective modules and singularity categories, and give combinatorial descriptions of the equivalences for almost gentle algebras using marked configurations.

title: A normalization issue in a transmitted form of Bloch's diamond formula: anti-invariant subgroup versus regulator quotient
comment: 12 pages. Verification script and run log included as ancillary files; companion code archive at https://github.com/huiminZheng-collab/boyd-conductor11 and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21820650 (scripts for the 11.a3 curve). Research carried out with the assistance of the AI system Kimi (Moonshot AI); see the declaration in the article
summary: Bloch's identity $\int_γη(f,g)=D_E((f)\diamond(g))$, relating the regulator of a $K_2$-symbol on an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ to the elliptic dilogarithm of the diamond product of the divisors, is transmitted in the Mahler-measure literature with $γ$ generating the anti-invariant subgroup $H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})^-$ and factor $1$ (e.g. Lalin-Ramamonjisoa, Thm. 6). We observe that, when $E(\mathbb{R})$ has one connected component ($Δ<0$), this reading is incompatible with the published intersection-product normalization (Brunault, Proposition 19): the anti-invariant subgroup then has index $2$ in the regulator quotient $H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})/H_1(E,\mathbb{Z})^+$. The correct statement -- factor $1$ for the quotient generator, hence factor $ι(E)\in\{1,2\}$ for the subgroup generator, with $ι(E)=1\iffΔ>0$ -- follows from Brunault's formula by an elementary index computation. We document the phenomenon twice: on 11.a3 by proved values (a Siegel-unit anchor from [Zheng, arXiv:2609.26119]; the diamond side by Brunault and Bertin), and on 20.a4 by high-precision computation of both integrals against the $q$-series for $D_E$ (subgroup/quotient ratio $2$ to $13$ digits). We also show that Touafek's Theorem 2 (involving a $Δ<0$ curve) mixes two independent normalizations (subgroup versus quotient, and a $(2π)^{-1}$ prefactor versus the bare diamond value), and we identify the two-part reinterpretation making its printed formulas mutually compatible. In the cases we have checked, no Mahler-measure or $D_E$-identity is affected: the main theorem of Lalin-Ramamonjisoa (conductor $17$, $Δ>0$) and Bertin's proved exotic relations stand untouched, and Touafek's final $D_E$-relation is not contradicted and is numerically supported, though its printed derivation retains the gap described in the text. A systematic audit is beyond the scope of this note.

title: Non-admissible smooth irreducible representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ for totally ramified extensions $F/\mathbb{Q}_p$
summary: Let $p\geq 5$, and let $F/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a nontrivial finite totally ramified extension. We construct a non-admissible smooth irreducible representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$. The construction uses representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathcal{O}_F)$ on which the first principal congruence subgroup acts nontrivially, together with a deformation of a diagram indexed by $\mathbb{Z}$.

title: Low moments of sums of extended Rademacher random multiplicative functions
summary:
Let $X^e \colon \mathbb{N} \to \{\pm 1\}$ be the random, completely multiplicative function whose values at the primes $(X^e(p))_{p \text{ prime}}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on $\{ \pm 1 \}$. Let $X=X^eμ^2$. We determine the order of magnitude of
  \[
  \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \bigg| \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\sum_{n \le x} X^e(n) \bigg|^{2 q} \Bigg]\quad \text{ and }\quad \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \bigg|\sum_{n \le x} \frac{X(n)}{\sqrt{n}} \bigg|^{2 q} \Bigg]
  \]
  for $q\in [0,1]$, showing that a transition from better-than-square-root cancellation to growth like a power of $\log x$ occurs when $q$ crosses $1/2$. In particular, the first absolute moments are of order $(\log\log x)^{3/4}$.
  The proof proceeds by comparing these sums to integrals of random Euler products, which are then studied by analogy with Gaussian multiplicative chaos integrals. The main difficulty lies in proving the lower bound at $q=1/2$, for which we also adapt arguments from the study of random walks.

title: Representation embeddings and the third Brauer--Thrall conjecture
comment: 24 pages, comments welcome! full Lean formalization of main results are available at https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/third-brauer-thrall-conjecture
summary: Let $A$ be a representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra over an algebraically closed field $k$. We prove that for every infinite cardinal $κ$ there is an indecomposable $A$-module $M$ with $\dim_k M=κ$. Over algebraically closed fields, this settles Simson's conjecture, also called the third Brauer--Thrall conjecture, that every representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra has indecomposable modules of arbitrarily large cardinality. To construct these modules, we extend Bongartz's representation embedding from finite-dimensional Kronecker modules without a simple injective summand to such modules of arbitrary dimension. The extended functor commutes with direct sums and filtered colimits and preserves the dimension of infinite-dimensional modules. Applying it to the indecomposable Kronecker modules of every infinite dimension constructed by Göbel and Simson yields the required $A$-modules.

title: On the existence of nonadmissible irreducible smooth representations of $p$-adic $\mathrm{GL}_n$
summary: Let $p>7$ be a prime, let $n>1$, and let $F$ be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic $p$ not equal to $\mathbb{Q}_p$. For every extension $E$ of the residue field of $F$, we construct an irreducible smooth $E$-representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ which is not admissible. When $E$ is countable, we also construct such representations without a central character and with nonscalar endomorphisms.

title: Arthur packets for $\mathrm{G}_2$ over $p$-adic fields
summary: We describe Arthur packets for the split reductive group $\mathrm{G}_2$ over a $p$-adic field and compute their stable and endoscopic character distributions. The construction uses the twisted Aubert duality recently studied by Cheng--Kaletha. We identify the corresponding Xu packets on $\mathrm{PGSO}_8$ and their triality-twisted characters. We also extend the result to long-root and short-root Arthur packets corresponding to unitary generic representations of $\mathrm{PGL}_2$.

title: Partitions with designated summands: $k$-tuples and their congruences
summary: Let $A_k(n)$ and $B_k(n)$ be the numbers of ordered $k$-tuples of partitions with designated summands, respectively with designated summands and all parts odd, of total size $n$. Using an exact description of the generating function of designated partitions after a $3$-dissection, we classify for every $e$ the values of $k$ for which $A_k(3n+2)$ is divisible by $3^e$: this happens exactly when $k\equiv0$ or $-5\pmod{3^e}$ if $e\le4$, and when $3^e\mid k$ if $e\ge5$. We obtain the corresponding exact $3$-adic and several $2$-adic results for $B_k$ and for $A_k$ along the progressions $4n+3$, a recursion for the classes $3^b(3n+s)$, and for $k=2$ the congruences $A_2(12n+10)\equiv 27f_1^4f_6^3/f_2\pmod{81}$ in generating-function form. We relate the numbers $A_k(n)$ modulo $3$ and $9$ to overpartitions, sums of squares and triangular numbers, give group-action proofs of some of the congruences, and close with several conjectures supported by computation.

title: On the existence of nonadmissible irreducible smooth representations of $p$-adic $\mathrm{GL}_n$
summary: Let $p>7$ be a prime, let $n>1$, and let $F$ be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic $p$ not equal to $\mathbb{Q}_p$. For every extension $E$ of the residue field of $F$, we construct an irreducible smooth $E$-representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$ which is not admissible. When $E$ is countable, we also construct such representations without a central character and with nonscalar endomorphisms.

title: Orbit Transversality for Projective Space
summary: Let $f\colon \mathbb{P}^n\to \mathbb{P}^n$ be a dominant endomorphism defined over a number field $K$. We show that there is a finite extension $L/K$ such that every proper closed subset of $\mathbb{P}^n$ misses at least one grand $(f,L)$-orbit. Equivalently, $(\mathbb{P}^n,f,K)$ is strongly dense orbit transversal (S-DOT): every set containing exactly one representative of each grand $(f,L)$-orbit is Zariski dense in $\mathbb{P}^n$.

title: Diophantine definability from addition and divisibility over rings of $S$-integers
summary: Let $K$ be a number field, let $S$ be a finite set of places of $K$ containing the archimedean places, and let $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$ denote the ring of $S$-integers of $K$. We prove that multiplication is positive-existentially definable in $(\mathcal{O}_{K,S},0,1,+,\mid)$ if and only if the unit group $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}^\times$ is infinite. This extends a 1977 theorem of Lipshitz for rings of integers to rings of $S$-integers. One of the key ingredients is a uniform bound for unit equations due to Evertse, Schlickewei and Schmidt, which we use to recover multiplication on the unit group.

title: Second moment of incomplete Eisenstein series revisited
summary: We revisit Yu's second moment formula for incomplete Eisenstein series and give uniform bounds for secondary terms appearing in this formula. We use these bounds to improve results on distribution of integer points on the light cone corresponding to an indefinite quadratic form, as well as intrinsic Diophantine approximation on ellipsoids, and counting holonomy vectors of saddle connections of Veech surfaces.

title: Collision Parameters in Higher-Dimensional Families of Polynomials
summary: Let $d\geq 3$ and consider the generic family of monic normalized polynomials $f_{\mathbf{t}}(z)=z^d+t_1z^{d-2}+t_2z^{d-3}+\cdots+t_{d-2}z+t_{d-1}$, where $\mathbf{t}=(t_1,\ldots,t_{d-1})$. Given pairwise distinct starting points $α_1,\ldots,α_d\in\bar{\mathbb{Q}}$ and a target point $β\in\bar{\mathbb{Q}}$, we show that the set of parameters $\boldsymbolλ\in\mathbb{A}^{d-1}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}})$ for which $β$ belongs to the forward orbit of every $α_i$ under $f_{\boldsymbolλ}$ is not Zariski dense in $\mathbb{A}^{d-1}$.

title: Twisted Diophantine approximation: asymptotic and uniform results
summary: Fix an $m\times n$ matrix $A$; twisted Diophantine approximation studies how well we can approximate the affine form $A {\bf q}-{\bf b}$ by an integer $m$-vector, depending on the choice of $m$-vector ${\bf b}$. We report on two companion papers in twisted Diophantine approximation, covering two setups: asymptotic and uniform. The asymptotic paper gives an exact Khintchine-type Lebesgue zero--one law, a null--conull criterion for badly approximable shifts, and Hausdorff-measure tests yielding exact power-law dimensions under a critical divergence condition. The uniform paper computes Hausdorff dimensions of sets of uniformly approximable vectors. It also gives Hausdorff zero--full laws, uniform-exponent spectra, and a sharp escape-of-mass bound. In both cases the results are established for arbitrary approximation functions from suitable regularity classes, and the arguments use a homogeneous lattice count involving all successive minima to record clustering in every independent direction.

title: A Rankin-Selberg Integral for $SU_{2,2}$
summary: We construct a Rankin-Selberg integral for the non-split quasi-split unitary group $SU_{2,2}$ and prove that it is Eulerian. We then compute the local integral at inert places where all data are unramified, and show that it represents the local adjoint $L$-function of $SU_{2,2}$.

title: Maximal Unipotent Monodromy and $p$-adic Eigenvalue Formulas
summary: We establish p-adic formulas for the eigenvalues of Frobenius in the case of the family of hyperkloosterman sums. The deformation equation in this case has maximal unipotent monodromy, and the interplay of Frobenius and the differential equation plays an important role in establishing p-adic analytic formulas for the eigenvalues.

title: The enhanced polylogarithm conjecture in weight two for imaginary quadratic fields
summary: Zagier's polylogarithm conjecture predicts that special values of Dedekind zeta functions can be expressed in terms of polylogarithms at algebraic arguments. For imaginary quadratic fields, Zagier and Gangl refined it by lifting both sides to complex values modulo rational multiples of a power of $2πi$. In previous work, the author extended their enhanced zeta values from ideal classes to ray classes by means of the Shintani $L$-function of two variables and formulated the enhanced polylogarithm conjecture for ray classes. In this article, we prove this conjecture in weight two. More precisely, we establish a Galois-equivariant equality between the enhanced partial zeta values of ray classes and the enhanced dilogarithms of elements of the rational Bloch groups of the corresponding ray class fields. These elements are constructed explicitly, starting from the Eisenstein class of Doran and Kerr on the square of a CM elliptic curve and contracting it with the graphs of complex multiplication.

title: Poissonian Pair Correlation and Discrepancy Rates
summary: We prove the existence of a sequence in $[0,1)$ with Poissonian pair correlation (PPC) and optimal-order star discrepancy $D_N^*=O((\log N)/N)$, and further give a deterministic construction by applying a conditional-expectation rule to a nested dyadic random model. We also show that PPC imposes no universal discrepancy decay rate: for every positive sequence $ρ_N\to0$, there exists a PPC sequence with $D_N^*/ρ_N\to\infty$. Under suitable regularity and growth assumptions, we realize prescribed discrepancy asymptotics, including $D_N^*\sim c_βN^{-β}$ for every $0<β<1$, with $c_β>0$. We further construct a PPC sequence satisfying $D_N^*\asymp(\log N)/N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: The Minimal excludant of $\ell$-regular partition
summary: Andrews and Newman \cite{andrewsnewmanI} introduced and studied ``mex,'' function for an integer partition $λ$ of a positive integer $n$. The related function $σ^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ was subsequently defined, and its generating function and other properties have been studied by several authors. In this article, for a positive integer $\ell \geq 2$, we define the minimal excludant of an $\ell$-regular partition $λ$ of a positive integer $n$. We then define $σ_\ell^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$, the sum of the minimal excludants over all $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$, and obtain explicit generating functions for $σ_\ell^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ in the cases $\ell = 2$ and $\ell = 3$, expressed as eta-quotients. We prove that the sequence $σ_\ell^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ is weakly increasing for every $\ell$, and we obtain Hardy--Ramanujan type asymptotic formulas for $σ_2^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ and $σ_3^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ as $n \to \infty$. Additionally, we completely determine the parity of $σ_2^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$, showing that it is odd precisely at generalized pentagonal numbers, and we use this characterization to compute the density of $n$ for which $σ_2^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$ is odd versus even. Finally, for $σ_3^{\mathrm{mex}}(n)$, we prove that it is odd infinitely often, and we establish a quantitative lower bound, showing that the number of such $n$ up to $X$ grows at least like $\log \log X$.

title: A Galois-type Springer theorem for hermitian and generalized quadratic forms
summary: We prove that anisotropy of nonsingular hermitian and skew-hermitian forms over central simple algebras with involution is preserved under scalar extension to every finite Galois extension of odd degree coprime to the index of the algebra. In characteristic two, the same conclusion holds for generalized quadratic forms over algebras with involution of the first kind, with no nonsingularity assumption on their polar forms. The main tool is an isometry-level descent theorem. For a cyclic extension of odd prime degree, every anisotropic nonsingular form over a division algebra with involution, of rank smaller than the extension degree and with Galois-invariant isometry class, descends to an anisotropic form over the base field. Unlike descent results for Witt classes, this theorem descends the form itself. A bounded-rank reduction, based on injectivity of the Witt-group restriction map, derives the cyclic anisotropy theorem from this descent result; a regularization argument removes the nonsingularity assumption on polar forms in characteristic two, and the Feit-Thompson theorem extends the result to arbitrary finite Galois extensions of odd degree.

title: Rational Torsion and Ramification Constraints on Odd Superelliptic Jacobians
summary: Let C: y^d = f(x) be a smooth projective superelliptic curve over Q, where d >= 3 is odd, f(x) in Q[x] is separable of degree n >= 3, and gcd(d,n) = 1. Let J = Jac(C) be its Jacobian. We study the rational torsion subgroup J(Q)_tors through the interaction of ramification geometry, Galois actions, reduction at primes of good reduction, and the geometry of divisors. First, we describe the subgroup R_d contained in J[d] generated by the ramification-point differences and determine its Galois-invariant subgroup explicitly in terms of the sizes of the Galois orbits of the roots of f. This yields a precise description of the rational d-torsion classes arising from ramification, without assuming that they account for all of J(Q)[d]. Second, we establish criteria based on the orders of reduced Jacobians that can prove the vanishing of the full rational torsion subgroup. Finally, we derive geometric constraints on divisor classes represented by effective divisors of degree smaller than the genus, including a restriction arising when distinct effective divisors represent the same class. Explicit examples illustrate how the Galois-theoretic and reduction-theoretic methods can be combined to study rational torsion on odd superelliptic Jacobians.

title: Certified Collision Exclusion and an Unconditional Upper Bound $Λ<0.156821$ for the de Bruijn--Newman Constant
summary: The de Bruijn--Newman constant $Λ$ is the transition time beyond which all zeros of the heat-deformed Riemann $ξ$-function are real. We develop a computer-assisted collision-exclusion method and obtain the bound $Λ<156821/10^6=0.156821$, in the normalisation of Polymath. The proof combines the published finite-height verification and the starting inequality $Λ\leq1/5$ with a compact-interior continuation theorem, five stable prime-polynomial Gram sources, certified moving-index recovery, a balanced real-jet transfer and a uniform Euler-product barrier at infinity. The resulting closed time-band exclusion, together with uniform remote reality, forces strictness at the proposed endpoint. The finite certificate uses 664,505 structural Fourier coefficients, 44,182 closed torus boxes, 184 separator moments and 17,385 separator rectangles. We isolate a Cauchy--Schwarz obstruction intrinsic to the four-prime source family, explaining the narrow feasibility margin of the certified endpoint. We state the proof-to-certificate interface and distinguish the present unconditional logical claim from other recent, as yet unrefereed, computational bounds.

title: Hopf-Galois Structures on Extensions Arising from Division Points on Elliptic Curves
summary: We provide a general construction of infinite Hopf-Galois extensions from a direct system of finite Hopf-Galois extensions. We then apply this framework to extensions generated by division points on elliptic curves. Specifically, for a number field $K$ and an elliptic curve $E/K$ of rank at least $1$ with $P\in E(K)$ of infinite order, we consider for each integer $n\geq 2$ the extension $L_n=K(Q_n)$, where $Q_n\in E(\overline{K})$ is such that $nQ_n=P$. We show that the finite-level extensions $L_n/K$ need not be Hopf-Galois, and we give sufficient conditions for them to be so. We then prove that the infinite extension $L_\infty=\bigcup_{n\geq 2}L_n$ of $K$ is potentially Hopf-Galois, meaning it becomes Hopf-Galois after a finite extension of the base field.

title: Multiple $q$-zeta values as polynomials in partition multiplicities
summary: Writing multiple $q$-zeta values as sums over partitions, a conjecture of Bachmann, proved by Hirose, Maesaka and Watanabe by means of a recursion, says that polynomials in the parts and multiplicities can be replaced by polynomials in the multiplicities alone. We make this replacement explicit, derive from it bounds on weight and depth that make Bachmann's conjecture effective, and provide a closed formula for the Drop1 operator of Hirose, Maesaka, Seki and Watanabe.

title: Private key sieves for improved attacks on RSA
comment: 12 pages, short version of the paper
summary: The RSA cryptosystem has been studied extensively and its insecurity in specific scenarios is well known. For instance, a sufficiently small private key allows to factorize the modulus $N$ and break the system. Attacks like this are often based on lattice reduction for finding small roots of polynomials, but high lattice dimensions can make it difficult to achieve the theoretically proved bounds in practice. In this paper, we adapt a sieve technique originally developed for deterministic integer factorization and apply it to RSA parameters. The sieve allows for an asymptotically significant reduction of the private key search space, and can be used to decrease the bounds for the polynomial roots. We also provide a square-root speed-up of the best currently known runtime bound for factoring semiprime $N=pq$ with small prime difference $q-p$.

title: Improved deterministic integer factorization by quadratic-image sieving
summary:
Let $N=pq$ be a semiprime and let $\ell\nmid N$ be an odd prime. For $a\ne0$ modulo $\ell$, put $H_a(N;\ell)=\{ax+Nx^{-1}:x\in\F_\ell^*\}$. For a primitive root $γ$, the size of $H_γ(N;\ell)\cup H_{γ^2}(N;\ell)$ is determined by the Frobenius trace of $Y^2=(X^2-1)(X^2-γ)$. We study the resulting trace-selection problem through finite certificates, a congruence modulo $8$, and a GRH-conditional positive-density family from the CM specialization $γ=2$.
  Independently of this conditional result, we obtain a deterministic factorization algorithm from the residue-known coefficient lattice of Harvey and Hittmeir (\emph{Math. Comp.}, 2022). The actual babystep index is a nondegenerate quadratic image modulo each selected prime divisor of the auxiliary modulus. After a computable translation, every such image avoids a fixed set of $(\ell-χ(-1))/4$ residues. This forbidden set is optimal among translated sets that must handle both square classes of the leading coefficient. Gauss reduction, a nearby lattice-vector selection, arbitrary-point multipoint evaluation, and the unrestricted large-order algorithm of Harvey and Hittmeir (arXiv, 2026) give the bit-complexity bound $N^{1/5}\exp(-(\log(4/3)/50+o(1))\log N/\log\log N)$. Its secondary factor is asymptotically smaller than every fixed negative power of $\log N$, improving the general bound of Harvey and Hittmeir (\emph{Math. Comp.}, 2022) and the balanced-semiprime bound of Gao et al.\ (arXiv, 2025).

title: Unit fraction representations using shifted Golomb primes
summary: We prove that every positive rational number is a sum of distinct unit fractions with denominators of the form $g-h$, where $g$ is a Golomb prime and $h$ is a fixed nonzero integer, as long as the necessary congruence conditions are satisfied. Golomb primes, introduced by Golomb in 1955, are a natural analogue of the primes. Erdős showed that the relative density of Golomb primes among the primes up to $N$ is about $1/\log\log N$, so they form a sparse subset of the primes. Our result is an analogue of Bloom's result on unit fraction representations using shifted primes, for this sparse subset of the primes. A key ingredient in our proof is a Siegel--Walfisz-type theorem for Golomb primes in arithmetic progressions, which we also prove here.
